title: God is light (1 John 1:5–10)
hook: if we confess, he is faithful to forgive

segments.voice: Yesterday: the opening of First John, and fellowship, a shared and common life. Your line was joy made full.

Walk into a dark room and flip on the light. The first thing you see is not the furniture. It's the mess: the clothes on the chair, the dust on the shelf, the mug you forgot. In the dark, the room seemed fine. In the light, it's honest. That's why some of us prefer dim lighting. Today's passage starts with a statement about God that is three words long in English, and then moves straight to what happens to our mess when that light comes on.

In the King James Bible: "God is light, and in him is no darkness at all." No shadows in the corners, nothing half-true. Then the conclusion: if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another. Light is also about honesty between people. Then a run of ifs, like doors. If we say we have fellowship with God while walking in darkness, we lie. And: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us." The danger isn't having a mess; the letter takes for granted that there is one. The danger is saying there isn't. Then the open door: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness." The Greek word for confess is built from same and say: to say the same thing, to agree. To confess is to finally say about your life what God already says about it, what the light already shows. And the response isn't a lecture. It's faithful and just. Faithful, because God keeps his promise to forgive. Just, because the letter has just said that the blood of Jesus cleanses from all sin. Churches practice confession differently. Catholic and Orthodox Christians confess to God in the presence of a priest, in the sacrament of confession or reconciliation. Many Protestants confess privately to God, or together in a prayer of confession during worship, and some confess to a trusted friend.
screen: `CONFESS: SAY THE SAME AS THE LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Picture a lamp coming on in a room inside you, and let it shine on one thing you've done, or not done, that you've been avoiding. Name it plainly, without excuses and without beating yourself up, saying the same thing the light says. If you pray, say it to God and rest in the words faithful and just to forgive; if you don't, sit a moment in the relief of not pretending.
Confession. Saying the same thing about your life that the light already shows, and finding God faithful to forgive.
Your line: faithful to forgive. The light shows the mess, and the door stays open. Rest well.

howItsDone: Catholic and Orthodox Christians confess sins to God in the presence of a priest in the sacrament of confession; some Protestant services include a spoken prayer of confession, sometimes introduced with 1 John 1:8–9, followed by words of forgiveness.

chat.says: If God already knows everything I've done wrong, what's the point of confessing?
options: Confess means 'say the same': you agree with what the light shows, and God forgives.
It's how you earn forgiveness: the more you list, the more points God gives you.
There isn't one. If you say you have no sin, you can skip it.
chat.meaning: To confess is to say the same thing the light already shows. The letter says God is faithful and just to forgive.
